title: Flexbox & Grid Layouts
description: Build any layout you can imagine. Master CSS Flexbox for one-dimensional arrangements and CSS Grid for two-dimensional page structure — the two most important CSS features of the decade.
learningObjectives: Align and distribute items along one axis with Flexbox
Use flex-grow, flex-shrink, and flex-basis to control item sizing
Build two-dimensional layouts with CSS Grid
Define grid tracks using fr, auto, repeat(), and minmax()
Combine Flexbox and Grid to build real page layouts

sections.content: Setting display: flex on a container makes all direct children flex items. The key axis concepts: the main axis (row by default) and the cross axis (perpendicular). justify-content controls distribution along the main axis; align-items controls alignment on the cross axis.

exercises.question: Which property centers flex items both horizontally AND vertically inside a flex container?
options: Both justify-content and align-items set to center
exercises.correctAnswer: Both justify-content and align-items set to center
exercises.explanation: justify-content: center centers on the main axis (horizontal in row mode). align-items: center centers on the cross axis (vertical in row mode). You need both to center in both dimensions.

sections.content: 🎯 flex: 1 is the magic shorthand for 'fill remaining space equally'. Use flex: 0 0 auto for fixed-size items.

exercises.question: A flex container has two items. One has flex: 1, the other flex: 2. How is the remaining space distributed?
exercises.explanation: flex: 1 and flex: 2 creates a 1:2 ratio. Total parts = 3. First item gets 1/3 ≈ 33%, second gets 2/3 ≈ 66% of available space.

sections.content: CSS Grid is a two-dimensional layout system. You define rows and columns on the container; children automatically or explicitly place themselves into the resulting cells.

exercises.question: What does repeat(auto-fit, minmax(250px, 1fr)) do?
options: Creates columns that are always 250px wide
Creates as many 250px+ columns as fit, filling remaining space
exercises.correctAnswer: Creates as many 250px+ columns as fit, filling remaining space
hints: auto-fit fills available space, minmax sets constraints
exercises.explanation: auto-fit places as many columns as fit in the container. minmax(250px, 1fr) means each column is at least 250px but grows to fill available space. This creates a responsive grid with no media queries.

exercises.question: What does grid-auto-flow: dense do?
options: Fills empty gaps left by large spanning items with later items
Sets all rows to the same height
exercises.correctAnswer: Fills empty gaps left by large spanning items with later items
hints: Dense packing tries to fill every empty cell
exercises.explanation: dense instructs the grid algorithm to backtrack and fill holes left when wide items skip cells. Items may appear out of source order visually — good for image galleries.

exercises.question: Which layout system is best suited for a two-dimensional page layout with both defined rows and columns?
hints: One system is 1D, the other is 2D
exercises.explanation: CSS Grid is designed for two-dimensional layouts where you control both rows and columns. Flexbox is 1D — it manages items along a single axis (row or column).

capstoneProject.title: Dashboard Layout
capstoneProject.description: Build a complete admin dashboard layout using CSS Grid for the page structure and Flexbox for component-level alignment.
requirements: Grid holy-grail page layout: fixed sidebar, header, main, footer
Responsive: single column on mobile, sidebar layout on desktop
Stats row: 4 equal-width card grid using Flexbox with gap
Chart area: Grid with a wide main chart and narrow supporting charts
Recent activity table: full-width, inside the grid main area
Sidebar nav: vertical Flexbox with space-between and icon+label items
All using grid-template-areas for readable code
